title: Election Day Is Off to a Funny Start
author: Ken Klippenstein
content:

West Phoenix

 _Justice Department "Election Monitors" at a Maricopa County polling site in
West Phoenix_

E-Day is here, and there have already been two hilarious federal law
enforcement faceplants.

A federal judge ruled last night that the Trump administration's Justice
Department "election monitors" can't carry guns, wear uniforms, flash federal
badges, or arrest anyone. So they're basically glorified mall cops. ("Poll
Blart," as someone online
[wisecracked](https://bsky.app/profile/fubarobserver.bsky.social/post/3mzgxieaefs26).)

The next faceplant involves me, the FBI, and Connecticut's Secretary of the
State.

On Monday, the FBI's New Haven field office posted a brag about how "the FBI
protects the integrity of elections." But the post began with an unfortunate
blooper, "Election day is Wednesday…"

You read that right: the FBI, in an official post touting its work protecting
the sanctity of the vote, falsely told people the election would be Wednesday.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!7UUJ!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-
post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F237ff5c4-219c-42e3-9cfa-f1fd35c5987e_1206x1942.jpeg)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!7UUJ!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-
post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F237ff5c4-219c-42e3-9cfa-f1fd35c5987e_1206x1942.jpeg)The
FBI's post (since deleted)

Federal elections are always Tuesdays! That's been the law since 1845. Isn't
the FBI supposed to know a thing or two about the law?

When I stumbled across the post on X (nee Twitter) just before midnight, I was
amazed to see that the FBI wasn't being ridiculed for it. In fact, no one
seemed to have noticed it at all.

Readers who recall [my history](https://www.kenklippenstein.com/p/fbi-visits-
me-over-manifesto) with the FBI won't be surprised that I wasn't feeling
especially gracious and took the opportunity to blast the Bureau's fuckup
across every social platform I could think of. Thinking I had done my duty to
make at least a few people aware of this hilariously ironic blooper, I went to
bed laughing at the whole thing.

When I woke up, I was stunned to see that my post had triggered a minor public
outrage. [Raw Story](https://www.rawstory.com/midterm-
elections-2026-2678197341/), [Snopes](https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/fbi-
office-election-day-post/), [IBTimes](https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/fbi-new-haven-
office-wrong-election-day-date-1829808), the [New Haven
Independent](https://www.newhavenindependent.org/2026/11/03/fbi-typo-prompts-
sec-of-state-rebuke/) and the [Yale Daily
News](https://yaledailynews.com/articles/new-haven-heads-to-the-midterm-polls)
all picked it up. Best of all, Connecticut's secretary of the state, Stephanie
Thomas, issued a [press
release](https://www.einpresswire.com/article/954246632/statement-from-
connecticut-secretary-of-the-state-stephanie-thomas-on-misinformation-
circulating-about-the-date-of-election-day) warning voters about
"misinformation circulating on social media, posted by the FBI's New Haven
office." Her invocation of a national security buzzword like "misinformation"
was an especially funny twist of the knife, given the FBI's penchant for the
term.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!kLwH!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-

post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F090519f5-729d-4776-8bdf-19bc6f5c7f39_2144x1406.png)

The FBI was even made to comment, with a spokesperson saying only: "The post
was removed once the typo was identified."

Yeah, we noticed!

Both of these stories -- the mall-cop monitors and the FBI's New Haven gaff --
depict the national security system as I've come to understand it over the
past decade covering it. These guys aren't all-powerful. They're not even all-
competent!

That doesn't mean there's nothing alarming about them. I've spent the past
month documenting the real stuff: the [Pentagon
mobilizing](https://www.kenklippenstein.com/p/military-mobilizes-for-upcoming-
elections) against "foreign" election threats, [Cyber Command's Task Force
Raider](https://www.kenklippenstein.com/p/how-the-military-will-hack-the-
election) and its role in the midterms, the [National Guard's election
mission](https://www.kenklippenstein.com/p/exclusive-national-guards-
election), the feds' [planning for an election
"doomsday"](https://www.kenklippenstein.com/p/feds-prep-for-election-doomsday-
scenario), the government [branding a Senate candidate a national security
threat](https://www.kenklippenstein.com/p/el-sayed-is-national-security-
threat), and the White House [treating speech itself as election
interference](https://www.kenklippenstein.com/p/white-house-sees-speech-as-
election).

The military inserting itself into our election process is worth criticizing.
But criticizing is different from panicking. The people running these efforts
are the same people who can't remember elections are on Tuesdays.

Fear is what they're selling. Don't buy it.

Instead, why not laugh it off with us in the live chat tonight?
